THESIS "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003ETitle: CLINICAL PROFILE, ETIOLOGICAL FACTORS AND OUTCOMES OF ADULT ONSET SEIZURES\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENEED FOR STUDY :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGlobally, seizures are common disorders recognized since antiquity and are encountered frequently during medical practice; up to 10% of general population experience at least one seizure in their lifetime with the highest incidence occurring in early childhood and late adulthood. Seizures beginning in the adult life require special attention as regards to their etiology because these are likely to be due to an identifiable cause. These are mainly due to trauma, central nervous system (CNS) infections, space-occupying lesions, cerebrovascular accidents (CVA), metabolic disorders, and drugs. On the other hand, seizures beginning in childhood are more likely to be idiopathic. In addition, the etiology and clinical profile of seizures in adults necessitate decisions about the initiation and discontinuation of pharmacotherapy that are different from those in younger patients\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EINTRODUCTION:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA seizure is a sudden, uncontrolled burst of electrical activity in the brain. It can cause changes in behavior, movements, feelings and levels of consciousness. Having two or more seizures at least 24 hours apart that don't have a known cause is considered to be epilepsy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere are many types of seizures, and they have a range of symptoms and severity. Seizure types vary by where they begin in the brain and how far they spread. Most seizures last from 30 seconds to two minutes. A seizure that lasts longer than five minutes is a medical emergency.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESeizures can happen after a stroke or a head injury. They also may be caused by an infection such as meningitis or another illness. Many times, though, the cause is unknown.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENerve cells in the brain, known as neurons, create, send and receive electrical impulses. This allows the cells to communicate. Anything that disrupts the communication pathways can lead to a seizure. Some types of seizures may be caused by genetic changes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe most common cause of seizures is epilepsy. But not every person who has a seizure has epilepsy. Sometimes seizures may be caused or triggered by:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA high fever. When this happens, the seizure is known as a febrile seizure.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAn infection of the brain. This may include meningitis or encephalitis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESevere general illness, including a severe infection of COVID-19.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELack of sleep.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELow blood sodium. This can happen with medicine that makes you urinate.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECertain medicines that treat pain, depression or help people stop smoking. They can make it easier for seizures to happen.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA new, active brain injury, such as head trauma. It can cause bleeding in an area of the brain or a new stroke.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe use of legal or illegal drugs that may be sold on the streets, such as amphetamines or cocaine.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAlcohol misuse, including during times of withdrawal or extreme intoxication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMost seizures can be controlled with medicine. However, managing seizures can affect your daily life\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAIM: To analyse the clinical profile, etiological factors and outcomes in patients with new onset seizures in adults\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOBJECTIVES:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. To assess the clinical profile of patients with new onset seizures\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. To study the underlying etiological factors that cause seizures\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. To study the patient centred outcomes in patients with new onset of seizures\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMATERIALS AND METHODS\u003Cb\u003E :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPLACE OF STUDY : Department of General Medicine, Kamineni Institute of Medical Sciences, Narketpally.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESTUDY PERIOD : november 2023-october 2025\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESTUDY DESIGN : Prospective Study, Observational study\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESAMPLE SIZE\u003Cb\u003E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo.of cases to be studied =50\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1.
